A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LTE research work. All 12 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3-4B/8B training experiments, results on six mathematical benchmarks, and training-dynamics analyses in Tables 1 and 3 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, training-dynamics analyses and component ablations in Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–5.

M1.justification: The hinted extra rollouts, truncation-dependent prompts, replacement with successful responses and mixed-policy objective remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical apart from terminology. LTE† renames the existing entropy-enabled variant; the new ablations test existing components.

E1.justification: Training coverage changes from separate difficulty-selected Skywork-OR1-RL-Data subsets for the two models to a common OpenR1-Math-46k-8192 corpus. This replaces the central training data, while mathematical reasoning and all six evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add evaluated EvoCoT, ReLIFT, DAPO and LUFFY comparisons for both model sizes. The entropy-enabled GRPO and GRPO-plus-extra-rollout comparisons disappear. GRPOExtra is the renamed existing extra-rollout baseline, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: Training changes from 300 to 500 steps and from a 16,384-token to an 8,192-token response limit; final-checkpoint evaluation changes accordingly. Model-specific difficulty subsets are replaced by the common 45,792-instance corpus. v2 also introduces separate hint-removal controls for the 8B ablation. Benchmark sampling and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 and Table 3 isolate incorrect-answer hints and overlong-response hints, providing component-specific evidence absent from v1. Training-sample and dynamics analyses are revised for the new experiments, while v1's all-pass sample analysis and Figure 3c are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain four or sixteen sampled responses per evaluation problem and report point estimates. Neither supplies independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The confidence-level discussion in Appendix A is theoretical, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Most trained-model results are replaced: for example, entropy-free 8B LTE averages are 41.11/53.87 for Pass@1/Pass@k in v1 versus 49.01/66.78 in v2. These use different training conditions and are not same-setting gains. New baseline and ablation results appear, and GRPO's average Pass@k changes from below to above the base models.

T1.justification: v2 removes Appendix A.3's entire information-gain argument and Equations 22–25. Appendix A.2 removes the left-hand exponent n from Equation 19 and changes the stated assumption from alpha ~ Omega(1) to alpha > Omega(1/n). These alter both the scope and premises of the theoretical support.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the performance claim beyond GRPO variants to external-guidance methods, notably LTE† outperforming LUFFY under aligned settings. v2 qualifies independence as absence of explicit reasoning-trace guidance. The conclusion drops its contrast-optimization claim and categorical reward-hacking-free wording.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the missing-entropy-control limitation with the 8,192-token training limit. It removes the small-data/overfitting explanation for weaker 8B results, tentatively attributes poor EvoCoT/ReLIFT results to model compatibility, and explains Qwen2.5/Llama exclusions. The central interpretation of LTE promoting exploration remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-access information, host hardware and operating-system details, eight H20 GPUs, training times of roughly 6–9 days, and artifact licenses. Appendix B updates training hyperparameters and specifies LUFFY's entropy coefficient. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation; the hardware information is newly disclosed, not an established hardware change.

R1.justification: Related work adds reasoning hints from Chen et al., theorem-proving feedback from Thakur et al., and offline mistakes from Alazraki et al. Model-selection discussion adds Qwen2.5, Llama and contamination references; Yue et al. is removed. The four related-work categories and basic self-generated-guidance positioning remain.

P1.justification: The overall section order and methodological exposition remain largely intact. v2 standardizes terminology and variant names, edits the introduction and results narrative, adds a learning analogy, and condenses related-work and conclusion prose. A dedicated ablation subsection and expanded ethical-considerations paragraphs provide bounded structural additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds an introductory illustration and ablation/license tables, restructures the main result tables with an entropy-control column, and removes the training-statistics table. Training plots receive revised axes and legends; the all-pass panel disappears and the entropy plot focuses on the late-training range. Existing framework and prompt diagrams are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support through direct hint-component ablations and comparisons with advanced and external-guidance methods, addressing important gaps in v1's validation. New code-access and computational details improve reproduction guidance, and the abstract's GRPO margins now match the tables. Losing entropy-enabled GRPO comparisons and unresolved EvoCoT/ReLIFT compatibility concerns limit the evidence, but the added component and comparative tests provide a substantial net gain. Higher cross-version scores alone do not establish improvement because training conditions changed.
